newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scitex strives to restore profits.
newsitem.headline: Scitex strives to restore profits.

text.p: Scitex Corp's top priority is to restore the company to profitability although this is not likely to happen this year, company president and chief executive Yoav Chelouche said.
"Our utmost priority is to take care of profits," Chelouche told Reuters in an interview.
Once the flagship of Israel's high-tech sector, the maker of digital printing and digital video systems has seen its shares fall from $44 in 1992 to its current $10-5/8.
Chelouche would not give a time frame for when he expected the company would return to profitability. But when asked whether this could happen in the fourth quarter, he said it was not likely.
On Friday the company announced that its third-quarter operating loss would be significantly greater than its $11 million loss in the second quarter.
Scitex is due to announce third-quarter results on November 6. Israeli newspapers reported the loss could be as high as $60 million but Chelouche said he could not comment.
Scitex said revenue for its graphic arts division fell far short of expectations and it has commenced an extensive cost reduction programme including employee reductions and facility closures.
"There is a need for a turnaround in the graphic arts department. We need to match costs with demand," Chelouche said.
He blamed the revenue short-fall on market conditions.

"The graphic arts market is going through a transition period with changes in technology taking place. There is a general wait-and-see attitude. People are not sure whether to invest in current technology. The whole sector has seen a decline," he said.
Chelouche would not comment on newspaper reports that as many as 400 workers would be sacked from the division, which employs 2,500 worldwide.

Chelouche, who was to meet company workers on Monday to inform them of the planned reorganisation, said the layoffs would not be across the board. "We are not laying off people in the Far East or in customer support worldwide."
The layoffs will be in the United States, Europe and Israel.
Chelouche said the company's two other divisions -- digital printing and digital video -- would not be affected.
Chelouche also said the company was concerned with its share performance.

Earlier this year, Scitex rejected an offer from Israeli born entrepeneur Davidi Gilo to acquire the company for $25 a share in cash. The offer had caused the shares to shoot up to $21 a share, twice the present trading level.
